name: Banh nam
summary: A flat steamed rice dumpling in a banana leaf, filled with pork and shrimp and dipped in fish sauce. In Da Nang the 18 May 2020 city page groups bánh nậm with bánh bèo, bánh lọc, and bánh xèo, and the 12 Jun 2026 markets page names it at Con Market.
origin: Hue. Vietnam Tourism says the dumpling comes from the imperial court.
history: Vietnam Tourism says bánh nậm owes its origins to the imperial court: a flat steamed rice dumpling, pork and shrimp, wrapped in a banana leaf.
culture: It belongs with the small steamed cakes of the former capital. Vietnam Tourism sets it beside bánh bèo as a snack you finish with a few drops of fish sauce.
texture: The dumpling is a thin layer of rice flour, steamed until the sheet is flat and translucent, then folded in a banana leaf.
taste: The filling is minced pork and shrimp. Vietnam Tourism also describes shrimp fried with garlic and scallion. The dip is fish sauce.
howToEat: Dip the dumpling in fish sauce.
In Dong Hoi, bánh nậm is rice flour steamed 15–20 minutes, wrapped in lá dong, with a shrimp filling.
where: In Hue, eat it with the other small cakes.
In Da Nang, Con Market names bánh nậm on the 12 Jun 2026 page, at 290 Hùng Vương, with a printed window of 06:00–19:00. Older Da Nang clocks for the same hall do not match that window.
In Dong Hoi the cake is the Quảng Bình one, wrapped in lá dong with shrimp.
seoTitle: Banh nam in Hue — the banana-leaf dumpling
seoDescription: A flat steamed rice dumpling from the Hue court kitchen, pork and shrimp in a banana leaf, dipped in fish sauce.
